"Saturn at opposition" means that Saturn and the Sun are exactly on two sides of the Earth, and the three are almost in a straight line. This astronomical phenomenon occurs once every 378 days. Saturn and the Earth revolve around the Sun in the same direction, and their orbital trajectories are both approximately circular. The Earth's orbital period and radius around the Sun, as well as the gravitational constant, are all known. According to the above information, one can find (　　)
